name: LoRaWAN
label: LoRaWAN
notes: LoRaWAN, decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. One job reads every channel of one regional plan that lies inside its band: start it with a band of 2 MHz on the plan's channels (the handler takes 2 MHz of IQ, and exits at start when no channel plan has a channel inside the band; the plan is the one with the most channels inside). Each event is a frame with a good CRC, or a downlink that OnAir reads as LoRaWAN: `devaddr` (eight lower-case hex digits on a data frame; a join request has none, its EUIs are in `hex`), `hex` (the PHY payload as OnAir's bus spells it, upper-case byte pairs separated by spaces), `kind` (always `lorawan`), `modulation` (`lora` or `fsk`), `sf` (the spreading factor, 0 for an FSK frame), `snr_db` (in the LoRa bandwidth) and `freq_hz` (the channel's centre). Nothing is decrypted and no MIC is checked; the PHY payloads (behind a LoRaTap header, link type 270) go to a packet capture. Ranges and bands: the plans OnAir decodes (EU868, US915, AU915, AS923-1 to 4 and EU433) and so the ranges 433.05 to 434.79, 863 to 870 and 902 to 928 MHz are the LoRa Alliance's Regional Parameters (RP002); the channels are 125, 250 and 500 kHz wide, so a job may be as narrow as one 125 kHz channel, and a plan the receiver does not carry (IN865, KR920) is not decoded. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 0.24 of a core and the node 0.08 of a core (load average 7.8 to 6.5, with another build running).
